newsitem.title: THAILAND: Moody's to review Thai banks, downgrade expected.
newsitem.headline: Moody's to review Thai banks, downgrade expected.

text.p: Moody's Investor Services said on Monday it would review the credit ratings of three Thai commercial banks, and analysts consider a downgrade inevitable given Thailand's deteriorating financial fundamentals.
The U.S.-based ratings agency said it planned a review and possible downgrade of its ratings for Bank of Ayudhya Plc, Siam City Bank Plc and Thai Military Bank Plc.
The review of the three medium-sized banks was prompted by Thailand's weakening financial fundamentals, declining property and stock markets, it said.
A deepening crisis in the finance company sector and Thailand's continuing economic slowdown were also cited by the agency as worrying factors.
"The rating agency noted that the anticipated drop in property values will have direct implications for the reserve levels of Thai Banks," the statement said.

Moody's recently annouced that it was placing Thailand's A2 long term sovereign credit rating under review. It announced a review of the credit ratings and possible downgrade for the top four Thai banks at that time.

"I think the reasoning for the review of these banks is based on the current country's review. If the country rating comes down they all have to come down," said a bank analyst at a Bangkok Bank affiliate.
Two Moody's officials were in Bangkok last week to meet senior officials and review national economic data for a decision on the review which is expected in two months time.
Under Moody's regulations a country's rating must be higher than that of any of that country's institutions.
Bank of Ayudhya currently has a Baa1 deposit rating. Siam City Bank and Thai Military Bank have Baa2 deposit ratings.

A downward revision of ratings would add approximately 50-100 basis points to funding costs, and would move Siam City Bank and Thai Military Bank towards the agency's speculative rating band, analysts said.

Several research houses have said Thai Military Bank's profit potential would be adversely affected by more stringent provisioning requirements for sub-standard assets set by the Thai government last week.

"I think it is fair to say Thai Military has made some fairly chunky settlement of old bad debts recently, but the old ones need to be settled because of a risk of new ones appearing. It's something of a race between these two factors," said Alistair Macdonald, banking analyst at Asia Equity.

With Moody's citing turmoil in the finance sector as a reason for the review, Siam City Bank's close association with affiliate Siam City Credit Finance and Securities (SCCF) amid a slump in the local stock market and difficult lending conditions will be a concern for the agency, analysts said.
The market had lost around 50 percent of its value in the past 12 months and there are worries about the quality of SCCF's loan portfolio, they said.
Bank of Ayudhya has a relatively higher percentage of provisioning to cover non-performing assets, analysts said.
But they added that investor doubts now persisted about all but the very biggest bank's ability to cope with a prolonged deterioration in the operating environment in Thailand.
Despite the Moody's statement, Bank of Ayudhya shares were up 2.00 baht at 53 at 0500 GMT. But Thai Military Bank shares dropped 1.25 to 36.25 baht and Siam City Bank was unchanged at 19.25 baht.
